cases.name: a-formula-over-two-columns
cases.description: Arithmetic over the columns beside it, one column out. The point of the case is that the two engines fetch a sibling from different places — an array in memory, a resolve(i) when streaming — and must still agree.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="bmi" local="en"><sequence name="W"><gen type="number" value="60..90"/></sequence><sequence name="H"><gen type="number" value="150..190"/></sequence><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="formula" expr="W * 10000 / (H * H)" decimals="1"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{W}} ${{H}} ${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-formula-counts-the-row
cases.description: _count is the row number, one-based, and it is a NUMBER rather than text — so multiplying it is arithmetic and not repetition.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="cnt" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="formula" expr="_count * 3"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-formula-adds-fractions-instead-of-joining-them
cases.description: `+` between two fractional values is addition. It used to concatenate — 0.5 + 0.25 came out "0.50.25" — and nothing warned, so this case exists to keep the easy thing pinned as well as the hard ones.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="add" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="formula" expr="0.5 + 0.25"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-formula-leaves-an-empty-source-empty
cases.description: A cell a parent= filter switched off is not a zero, so the formula that reads it answers with nothing rather than with 0. Both engines, same rule.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="mask" local="en"><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F"/></sequence><sequence name="S" parent="G.M"><gen type="number" value="7..7"/></sequence><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="formula" expr="S * 2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{G}} ${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-fan-out-with-a-declared-shape
cases.description: lengths= is a whole-run quota over how many values each row gets: 50% of the rows one value, 30% two, 20% three. Not approximately — exactly, laid out by the same Hamilton arithmetic percent= uses.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="fan" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="number" value="1..9" repeat="1..3" lengths="50,30,20" separator=";"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-distribution-parameter-that-follows-another-column
cases.description: lambda reads a column instead of holding a number. How many uniforms a row spends depends on WHICH distribution and never on its parameters, so the row stays computable on its own and every engine agrees.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="traffic" local="en"><sequence name="T"><gen type="number" value="10..40"/></sequence><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="number" distribution="poisson" lambda="T * 0.1"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{T}} ${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-spread-that-drifts-over-the-run
cases.description: sd is an expression over _count, so the noise grows as the run goes on — an ageing sensor, with no feature of its own.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="drift" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="number" distribution="normal" mean="100" sd="0.1 + 0.5 * _count" decimals="2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-distribution-parameter-that-reads-an-empty-cell
cases.description: Nothing to draw from, so nothing is drawn: the row comes out empty, the way a formula answers the same input. The skipped row still spends the uniforms a drawn row would, so blanking a cell cannot slide the rest of the column.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="pfilter" local="en"><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F"/></sequence><sequence name="H" parent="G.M"><gen type="number" value="5..5"/></sequence><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="number" distribution="poisson" lambda="H"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{G}} ${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>
